shape.description: Half ring, ends two cells apart. Two arcs of slots. Open flat band with low side walls and long slots in the floor; tongue with small slot at each end, hooked foot under it.
shape.sizeBasis: Scaled from the floor cell (about 45 mm, one block width) against VTech parts drawings and Joey's photos; +-10%. No ruler in any photo. Track width about 25 mm (straights) and 31 mm (curved bands), read against block width in IMG_0952/0953 and lp manual p5.

accepts: block cup end (top notch or joint hole) with its side tab
block cup end (top notch or joint hole) with its side tab

physics.behaviour: Level 180 degree U-turn between two equal ports. Slows a marble by rubbing the outer wall.

evidence.shows: blue h2 to orange B-02 h2
both ends then roofed by B-04, so they sit at joint holes
T-02 tail on blue, equal height

assumptions: Connection: the track end is a thin tongue that overlaps the next piece. A small slot in the tongue takes a small peg on that piece, and a hooked foot under the end drops into the block's side tab (photos IMG_0959, 0963; foot on trex_plans_02).

Height finding: equal-height ports give a truly level track. Side elevations on trex_plans_02 draw T-06 horizontal, and iso rails on T-06 match the floor axis (0.66-0.69 vs 0.68-0.70 rise/run, read by eye, so a slope under about 0.1 slot per cell cannot be excluded). No built-in slope was found in blocks or straights. A marble crosses level runs on speed from an earlier drop, launcher or lift. It will not start from rest there.

Scale is estimated, not measured: one cell = one block width (top-down maps, trex_plans_27). A cell of about 45 mm is judged from hand and laptop-key size in IMG_0960/0963, +-5 mm. No ruler was in any photo.
